cards.front: Recall a key point about The Rise of the Nazis
cards.back: On 29 October 1929, the American stock market crashed (Wall Street Crash). American banks recalled loans from Germany, causing economic collapse. By 1932, 6 million Germans were unemployed (over 30% of the workforce), and industrial production fell by 58% from its 1929 level.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Rise of the Nazis
cards.back: In the 1928 election, the Nazis won just 2.6% of the vote (12 seats). By July 1932, they were the largest party with 37.3% of the vote (230 seats). This extraordinary rise was driven by the economic crisis and the failure of mainstream parties to solve it.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Rise of the Nazis
cards.back: The Nazis were NOT primarily a working-class party. Their strongest support came from the Protestant middle class, farmers, and small-town voters. The working class largely continued to support the SPD or KPD. However, the Nazis did make some inroads into the working class through the SA, which offered unemployed men food, comradeship and a sense of purpose.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Rise of the Nazis
cards.back: Joseph Goebbels was appointed Nazi Party propaganda leader in 1929. He controlled the Nazi message with extraordinary skill, using every available medium to reach the German people. He said: "The essence of propaganda consists in winning people over to an idea so sincerely, so vitally, that in the end they succumb to it and can never escape."

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Rise of the Nazis
cards.back: The SA (Brownshirts or Stormtroopers) was the Nazi paramilitary force, founded in 1921 and led by Ernst Röhm. By 1932, the SA had over 400,000 members - many of them unemployed men attracted by the uniform, comradeship, and regular meals.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Rise of the Nazis
cards.back: Hitler was appointed Chancellor on 30 January 1933 by President Hindenburg, not because he won a majority but because a group of conservative politicians believed they could control him. Franz von Papen famously claimed: "We've hired him" and "In two months, we'll have pushed Hitler so far into a corner that he'll squeak."

cards.front: What should you know about history exam tips — the rise of the nazis?
cards.back: 1. For The Rise of the Nazis, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with The Rise of the Nazis 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
